mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% compresses equity discount rates through accommodative monetary policy, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the policy stance remains accommodative.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4.5% occurs in 10 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand expansion, which precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise above their 90th percentile in the same month, yet S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL above 270) signals persistent price pressures that trigger aggressive monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during high inflation regimes.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL above 270 occurs in 15 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100.5 indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which correlates with higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 100.5 for 6 consecutive months and S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of those periods.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP level (GDPC1) exceeding 20000 billion dollars indicates strong economic expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: GDPC1 above 20000 occurs in 8 consecutive quarters and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of those quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals rapid labor market improvement, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through enhanced consumer spending momentum.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises in the same month, yet S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: During the post-pandemic recovery phase, rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve accelerates policy tightening to combat inflation.
failure_condition: In the post-pandemic recovery period (2021-01 to 2022-12), CPIAUCSL rises and S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the months.
